frontier.text: : build the mode-block coefficient modules so the Whitehead lemmas normalise an arbitrary loop cocycle to vanish on constant loops. Combined with the mode recurrence, this classifies central extensions of the polynomial loop algebra.

frontier.name: Current topology
frontier.text: : give formal currents the t-adic linear topology. Prove Hausdorffness, completeness, continuity of the bracket and density of polynomial currents, which is the prerequisite for every continuous statement in A1.

frontier.name: The extension ĝκ and h∨

status.glance: Only foundations exist so far. The finite-dimensional inputs to the A1 classification are proved: the Whitehead lemmas, the fact that invariant forms are multiples of the Killing form, and the polynomial mode recurrence. So are the first carriers for formal currents, the residue pairing and smooth modules. Nothing from the affine extension ĝκ onward has begun, and neither headline theorem has been started: the scalar center away from critical level and Feigin–Frenkel.

frontier.text: — the classical and cubical Hurewicz maps are known to differ by a universal unit of `ℤ`, but the sign itself is not determined. The roadmap's orientation conventions ask for it to be fixed.

frontier.text: — the spectral sequence of a filtered space exists with finite convergence, and fibre bundles give Serre fibrations. What remains is the skeletal filtration of the total space and `E² = H_p(B; H_q(F))` with monodromy. Bundle Euler multiplicativity waits on it.

frontier.name: Algebraic spectral sequences

status.glance: Van Kampen, relative singular homology, and excision with Mayer–Vietoris (Stages 1–3) are done. Manifold duality, the degree-`n` relative Hurewicz isomorphism, and every spectral sequence except the Čech one are still missing.

frontier.name: Multiplicative polynomial laws
frontier.text: (§0.DP.1) — define `PolynomialLaw.IsMultiplicative`, then prove that it is closed under composition and that degree-one multiplicative laws to `A` are algebra maps. This is self-contained, and the homogeneous half it mirrors is in place.

frontier.name: The universal homogeneous law `γ^univ_d`
frontier.text: (§0.DP.2) — construct the degree-`d` law `M → Γ^d_A(M)` with its coefficient formula. The grading it needs has landed, and every later Roby statement depends on it.

frontier.name: Roby representability and base change
frontier.text: (§0.DP.2) — show that `Hom_A(Γ^d_A(M), N)` is the module of degree-`d` homogeneous laws with no flatness assumption, and deduce `B ⊗ Γ^d_A(M) ≅ Γ^d_B(B ⊗ M)`. The prerequisite is `γ^univ_d`.

frontier.name: The Koszul complex of a finite sequence
frontier.text: (§0.K.1) — this has no dependence on the divided-power lane and can start now from Mathlib's exterior powers and regular sequences.

frontier.name: Mittag-Leffler and the six-term sequence for towers
frontier.text: (§1.T.1) — extend the existing `lim`/`lim¹` file with the Mittag-Leffler vanishing criterion and the long exact sequence of a short exact sequence of towers.

status.glance: The divided-power augmentation section (§0.DP.3) is done, and its two predecessors are partly done: homogeneous polynomial laws and the grading of the divided power algebra are in place, but multiplicative laws and Roby representability are not. Everything from the Koszul complex onward, including the cotangent complex, derived limits, completion, effectivity and Matlis duality, has not begun.

rows.name: EllipticCurves

frontier.name: Finiteness of `Sel_m`.
frontier.text: This needs finiteness of `H¹(G_{K,S}, E[m])`. The explicit 2-Selmer group is already finite, so comparing it with the cohomological `Sel₂` would give the case `m = 2`.

frontier.name: The rank of `y² = x³ − x + 1`.
frontier.text: Torsion is trivial and a general 2-descent rank bound exists. What remains is to apply the bound to this curve and exhibit a point of infinite order.

frontier.name: The Tate curve's uniformisation.
frontier.text: The coordinate series and their `q^ℤ`-periodicity are in place. Still unproved are that the series satisfy the Weierstrass equation, that they define a homomorphism, and the isomorphism `L^×/q^ℤ ≅ E_q(L)`.

frontier.name: Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich, converse directions.
frontier.text: These are unramified `T_ℓ` ⟹ good reduction and finite inertia image ⟹ potential good reduction, together with the `E[N]` criterion. Tamagawa numbers, with `c_v = [E(K) : E₀(K)]`, sit beside them.

frontier.name: The formal logarithm.
frontier.text: The formal group law and its torsion are in place, but neither the logarithm nor the exponential is defined.

status.glance: The Mordell–Weil theorem and the whole finite-field layer are proved, including the Hasse bound and rationality of the zeta function. Layers 0, 0.5, 2, 3, 4.5a and 4.5b are complete. Selmer groups and Sha are defined and sit in their exact sequence, but finiteness of the Selmer group, the Tate curve's uniformisation and the converse halves of Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich are still open.

rows.name: FinancialMathematics

frontier.name: Black–Scholes boundary and limit API.
frontier.text: This means the call and put values at `s = 0`, the far-field limits, the continuous extension to maturity by the payoffs, and gamma tending to `0` away from the strike and blowing up like `1/(Kσ√(2πτ))` at it. All of this is deterministic analysis on the existing closed forms.

frontier.name: Bond holdings and delta-hedge algebra.
frontier.text: This means the call and put bond holdings `b = −Ke^{−rτ}Φ(d₋)/β_t` and their put analogue. Combined with the PDE, these give the deterministic drift-matching statement the suggested file pins.

frontier.name: Uniqueness of the Black–Scholes price.
frontier.text: This means uniqueness in the linear-growth classical class via stopped Itô on `[1/n, n]` and GBM moment bounds. It needs Itô's formula and GBM moments from StochasticCalculus.

frontier.name: M0.1 asset and trading contracts.
frontier.text: This means the GBM/linear-SDE identification and the self-financing definition with its simple-strategy formula. It is blocked on StochasticCalculus S3 (stochastic integrals) and S9.4 (linear SDEs).

frontier.name: M0.2 completeness and no arbitrage.
frontier.text: This means the true-martingale density, the Brownian motion under `Q`, replication of `L²` claims, and the absence of arbitrage. It is blocked on StochasticCalculus S6.1 (martingale representation) and S7.4 (Girsanov), and on M0.1.

status.glance: The analytic core of M0.4 is in place: the closed-form call and put prices, their risk-neutral expectation formulas, put–call parity, the Black–Scholes equation and the Greeks. The stochastic market of M0.1–M0.3 has not begun. That market covers the asset SDE, self-financing trading, the equivalent martingale measure, completeness and replication.

rows.name: FormalLaurentPuiseux

frontier.name: Formal Newton–Puiseux root theorem (L5)
frontier.text: — Newton polygons and initial polynomials, the Tschirnhaus shift, ramify-and-rescale normalization, and the degree induction that splits off a coprime factor. The Hensel step it needs is in place, as are the common-level lift and the algebraicity needed to conclude algebraic closure.

frontier.name: Order-e residue formula and universal coefficient identity (L3)
frontier.text: — Res(f(φ)Dφ dt) = e·Res(f dt) for φ of order e in all characteristics, via the identity in ℤ[x₀,…,x_(ek)][x₀⁻¹]. Only the order-one case exists. AlgebraicCurves Layer 9 consumes this.

frontier.name: Puiseux valuation and topology (L4)
frontier.text: — restrict the Hahn additive valuation, prove the level embeddings are homeomorphisms onto their images, and exhibit Σ t^(j+1/(j+1)) as a Cauchy sequence with no Puiseux limit.

frontier.name: Vector- and Lie-valued Laurent series (L3)
frontier.text: — HahnModule ℤ K V with lattice topology, its continuous dual V*((t))dt, and the coefficient-convolution Lie algebra L((t)) compared with LieAlgebra.LoopAlgebra.residuePairing.

frontier.name: Kummer structure of the levels (L6)
frontier.text: — identify level n as the splitting field of X^n − t and consume Mathlib's Kummer theory; this waits on L5 for the finite-extension classification.

status.glance: The coordinate-level calculus on K((t)) (L1–L2) is essentially complete, and the Puiseux field has been built on its Hahn-series carrier together with its ramified levels, their degrees and its colimit presentation (L4, without valuation or differentials). L3 is partial. L5 has only its coprime-factor Hensel lemma, and the Galois layers L6–L7 have not begun.

frontier.text: Prove `H^q(X, F)` finite over a Noetherian base for proper `X`, and `R^q f_* F` coherent. The Čech comparison and the `ℙ¹` computation (genus zero, `H⁰(ℙ¹_R, 𝒪) = R`) are the starting points for the projective case. The proper case also needs Chow's lemma.

frontier.text: Semicontinuity, Grauert, and flat base change beyond two-affine covers. Layer D's twisted charts depend on these.

frontier.name: Representing `Pic⁰`.
frontier.text: Build the Hilbert quotient and projective Picard representability, then identify the result with the rigidified `Pic⁰` functor. This needs Hilbert schemes from SchemeAndStackFoundations §4.14 and the two items above.

frontier.name: `Symᵈ X` and the Abel maps.
frontier.text: Represent degree-`d` relative divisors by `Symᵈ X`. The degree-zero and degree-one cases and the affine-line chart are done. Then prove `AJ_d` surjective for `d ≥ g`.

frontier.name: Abelian-variety theory and the Albanese property.
frontier.text: The theorem of the cube, projectivity, duals and polarizations are all untouched. Abel–Jacobi as a morphism satisfying `IsAlbanese` waits on them and on representability.

status.glance: Layer A is done for curves. The curve case of Layer B is largely in place: Riemann–Roch, Serre duality through `Ω_{X/k}`, the Čech comparison and vanishing above degree one. General finiteness is not. The Picard functor now has its fppf sheaf, a `Pic⁰` subfunctor and an Abel–Jacobi map into it. Nothing is representable yet, so there is no Jacobian scheme. The abelian-variety theory beyond rigidity has not begun.

frontier.name: Planar cube edges are merges or splits.
frontier.text: Show that on a planar code each edge of the resolution cube either merges two circles or splits one. This needs the noncrossing consequence of the native Euler-characteristic `IsPlanar`, proved by the README's finite disc/band contraction argument.

frontier.name: Graded circle tensors and saddle maps.
frontier.text: Package `R[ε]` as the quantum-graded object `V`, build tensors indexed by finite circle sets with the enhanced-state basis, and assign `m` and `Δ` to the merge/split correspondences.

frontier.name: Completing the cube API.
frontier.text: Add the crossing-reordering chain isomorphism with subset-permutation signs, face restriction, height shifts and the mapping-cone description of the generic totalization.

frontier.name: The Khovanov complex and its Euler characteristic.
frontier.text: Apply the totalization to the actual resolution cube with the normalized shifts. Then prove `χ_q Kh(D;ℤ) = (q+q⁻¹)·eval(T↦−q, jonesPolynomial)` for nonempty diagrams, plus the separate empty-diagram case. This is blocked on the two items above.

frontier.name: The formal local cobordism category.
frontier.text: Construct the surface presentations, the cell-count grading and the `S`, `T`, `4Tu` quotient. This precedes the formal complexes in K3 and every Reidemeister homotopy in K4.

status.glance: Only the foundations have been laid, and only the first steps of K1, K2 and K3. These are the resolved-circle sets with their count, the Khovanov Frobenius algebra, and the generic signed cube totalization. No Khovanov complex of a diagram exists yet. Nothing for G or for K4–K7 has landed.

frontier.name: Almost every Eisenstein polynomial is separable
frontier.text: — show that the non-separable locus in the Eisenstein region is Haar-null, so that the pointwise root-count identity holds almost everywhere.

frontier.text: — derive AEMeasurable of each rootCount on the region from the local constancy already proved and the null non-separable locus.

frontier.name: The local fibre count
frontier.text: — Serre's Lemma 1: for ρ with d + n ≤ nρ, a monic g has exactly one root in the cube ξ + π^ρ𝒪_L iff ord g(ξ) ≥ nρ + d. The Hensel estimate and the box description of balls are its inputs; it also needs ord f′(ξ) = d for an Eisenstein generator.

frontier.name: The integral of the root count
frontier.text: — ∫ rootCount L = q^{−(d L + 1)}(1 − q^{−1}) over the region, by change of variables through the scaling law; needs the fibre count.

frontier.name: Theorem 1 and its corollaries
frontier.text: — interchange sum and integral to get ∑ q^{−c(L)} = n. Theorem 2 then follows from the orbit count and invariance of c, and the finite half of the dichotomy, convergence and the tame count come after it.

status.glance: The counting invariants (Layer 0), quantitative Newton lifting (Layer 1) and the lattice-index and Haar scaling layer (Layer 2) are done. Layer 3 is about half built: the Eisenstein region, its volume, countability and the pointwise root-count identity are in, but the fibre count and the integral are not. Of Layer 4, the orbit count and the infinite half of the finiteness dichotomy are proved; neither mass formula is.

status.glance: Only finite-group and diffeological groundwork for the local theory exists: the action-groupoid dictionary, finite Bochner linearization, invariant inner products, the linear generic-stabilizer theorem and quotient diffeologies. frontier.name: Conjugacy of maximal tori.
frontier.text: The general theorem exists conditionally: it assumes that diagonalizable subgroups can be conjugated into a reference torus. That hypothesis is discharged only for `GLₙ`, `SLₙ` and `Sp`. Borel conjugacy, together with the maximal torus inside each Borel, is the natural route to removing it.

frontier.text: Prove that distinct relevant torus images on the ray of A₀ are disjoint, by positivity and zero intersection. The independent-component expansion then identifies the ray-only count, and the conditional comparison with the full Gr series follows.

frontier.text: The theorem still treats a finite set of meromorphic singularities. Extending it to the paper's accumulation-free sets and to locally straight essential singularities lies beyond the pinned result.

frontier.name: Direct cycle geometry.
frontier.text: Propositions 2.2 and 2.3 are stated for one closed immersion. The cycle theory combines curve results additively, but no separately named cycle-level versions of these propositions are established here.

frontier.name: The valence formula.
frontier.text: The contour engine supplies the on-boundary winding weights, and an argument principle whose curve may meet the zeros. Assembling the modular valence formula remains work for the Modular Forms roadmap.

frontier.name: Signed-curvature packaging.
frontier.text: The crossing value is still expressed as `(ẋÿ − ẏẍ)/(2(ẋ² + ẏ²))` under `C²` regularity, as the roadmap intends. The supplied material identifies no general signed-curvature API to package it.

status.glance: The Hungerbühler–Wasem summit and all four supporting layers are established, for finite integral contour cycles as well as single curves. No layer is partial or untouched. What remains is generalisation beyond the roadmap's deliberately pinned scope.

frontier.name: Regulator lower bounds for positive unit rank
frontier.text: — the Layer-3 item proper. Everything present reduces to `R_K = 1` for a zero-dimensional unit lattice; no lower bound on the covolume exists for positive rank.

frontier.text: — the second half of Layer 3; not started.

frontier.name: `ZLattice` reconciliation of the engine
frontier.text: — the README asked that the packing and doubling API be mapped onto Mathlib's `ZLattice`/covolume before porting. The engine landed on additive subgroups of `ι → ℂ`; whether it also speaks to `ZLattice` is not established here.

frontier.name: Brauer–Siegel
frontier.text: — `log(h_F·R_F) ∼ log √|d_F|` with explicit constants; the long-horizon aspiration, untouched; it needs the Layer-3 regulator bounds.

status.glance: This roadmap lives under `Completed/`: the maintainers have declared it complete against its README, which records the Layer-1 explicit bounds, the explicit ideal count, the Layer-0 engine and the Layer-2 summit (an explicit count of number fields of bounded discriminant) as landed sorry-free. Layer 3 (regulators) has only its rank-zero base case, and the Brauer–Siegel horizon has not begun. The declaration list behind this snapshot under-represents the delivered work: each declaration is attributed to the commit that last touched it, and later consolidation of the `EffectiveBounds/` files moved much of the Layer-1 code out of this window.

frontier.text: — the successor roadmap: period domains as complex manifolds, Griffiths transversality, period maps and monodromy. It consumes the fiber datum, the period-domain points and the isometry group built here.

frontier.name: Tensor products and duals of mixed Hodge structures
frontier.text: — the mixed category has kernels, cokernels and products, but no dual, tensor product or internal Hom yet. This goes beyond the README.

frontier.name: A monoidal structure on the polarizable category
frontier.text: — tensor products, duals and internal Homs preserve polarizability, but the bundled category does not yet carry them as a monoidal or rigid structure. This also goes beyond the README.

frontier.name: Specializing onto Mathlib's filtration API
frontier.text: — the README's hook for `opposed`, `gradedF` and `gradedComplexEquiv` applies only if that in-progress Mathlib work lands.

status.glance: All four milestones are proved, and on the evidence here no target the README sets remains open. The pure theory now also has polarizations in the form the README prescribes, a fixed integral form with its complex form derived, and polarizability passes to duals and internal Homs. The mixed theory still has no tensor products or duals, and the successor roadmap on variations has not begun.

frontier.name: Kronecker–Weber beyond exponent two
frontier.text: — only multiquadratic fields and the genus field are placed in cyclotomic fields. The ClassFieldTheory roadmap plans the general case as a consequence of its global class field correspondence.

frontier.name: Hilbert and ring class fields
frontier.text: — untouched. Both rest on the existence theorem of class field theory, which the ClassFieldTheory roadmap plans to supply.

status.glance: All four layers are done. That covers the degree and Galois theory of multiquadratic fields, the decomposition law at every prime including a ramified 2, the genus field and the 2-rank theorem for real and imaginary quadratic fields, and every worked example the roadmap lists. Only the long horizon is open. Multiquadratic fields, the genus field and its totally real part are placed inside cyclotomic fields, but Kronecker–Weber for abelian fields of higher exponent and the Hilbert and ring class fields have not begun.

rows.name: NumberFieldArithmetic

frontier.name: Rank-one quartic fields
frontier.text: : the polynomial certificate needs prime degree, so a field such as `ℚ(ζ₈)` is outside it. The README excludes this case from scope, so extending the certificate is new work, not a missing milestone.

frontier.name: The class number of Dedekind's field
frontier.text: : the README deliberately claims no value. Claiming one would need a full Minkowski certificate with explicit generators for every prime below the bound.

frontier.name: The converse of the common-index-divisor obstruction
frontier.text: : Hensel's criterion, which says that the common index divisors are exactly the primes whose splitting type is not realisable modulo `p`, is excluded by the README and cited only.

frontier.name: Downstream consumers
frontier.text: : the Artin map, the relative discriminant and Dedekind's theorem are stable inputs for the class field theory and Chebotarev roadmaps. The density of split primes belongs to Chebotarev, not here.

status.glance: Every layer's milestones are proved, from the splitting dictionary to the worked invariant suite. Recent work has generalised the splitting dictionary to arbitrary Dedekind and integrally closed bases. What remains lies at the boundaries the README itself draws: higher-rank units, rank-one quartic fields, and anything that belongs to class field theory or Chebotarev.

rows.name: OrthogonalL2Bases

frontier.name: Multidimensional Fourier diagonalization
frontier.text: : the one-dimensional eigenrelation and the product basis are both in place, but their combination on `L²(ℝ^ι)` has not been stated.

frontier.name: Ladder operators on `L²`
frontier.text: : `a` and `a†` exist only on Schwartz space. On `L²` they are unbounded, so extending them needs closed-operator packaging rather than continuous linear maps. The README treats this as a downstream target, not a milestone.

frontier.name: Laguerre and Jacobi
frontier.text: : out of scope by design. The roadmap assigns them a separate future roadmap, and the families would have to be defined before any `L²` basis statement about them.

status.glance: Every part of the roadmap is done. The Hermite functions and the Chebyshev polynomials are complete orthonormal bases of their `L²` spaces. Both are built from one family-agnostic layer that also gives the weighted-measure and multidimensional bases. Each basis carries an explicit expansion and Parseval API. The Hermite basis also has its two main structural consequences: it diagonalizes the `L²` Fourier transform, and on Schwartz space it carries the ladder operators. What is left lies outside the roadmap's own targets.

frontier.name: The successor roadmaps.
frontier.text: The README assigns the following to successor roadmaps (`AlgebraicGroupStrongApproximation`, `ArithmeticReductionTheory`, `TamagawaMeasures`, `AdelicFourierAnalysis`), none of which is in the roadmap repository yet: - compact open families from integral models; - strong approximation and reduction theory; - Tamagawa measures and adelic Fourier analysis.

frontier.name: Continuity of the inverse sum splitting for other filters.
frontier.text: The inverse of the sum splitting is proved continuous in two cases: - for principal filters, with any reference family; - for the cofinite filter, with open reference subgroups.

frontier.name: Aliases once FLT's layer reaches Mathlib.
frontier.text: The README wants the ported change of factors, reindexing and eventual comparison lemmas to become aliases once FLT's second restricted-product layer is upstreamed.

status.glance: All four layers are done. Every export in the README's contract is proved, and rejection tests show which hypotheses cannot be dropped. The sum splitting now holds for an arbitrary filter, as the README asks. Nothing is partial or untouched. What comes next belongs to the roadmaps that consume this one.

rows.name: UniversalCovers

frontier.name: Higher homotopy of spheres, `RPⁿ` and lens spaces.
frontier.text: The covering isomorphism gives `π_k(RPⁿ) ≅ π_k(Sⁿ)` for `k ≥ 2`, but nothing here computes `π_n(Sⁿ)`; that needs a degree or Hurewicz argument, and neither appears here.

frontier.name: Existence of `K(G, 1)` spaces for an arbitrary group.
frontier.text: Only recognition is proved, with circles and tori as examples; constructing one for a given group rests on realization theory the README places outside this roadmap.

frontier.name: Bases without a universal cover.
frontier.text: The standing local hypotheses are shown to be exactly what a simply connected cover requires, so the classification cannot be pushed further as stated; spaces failing them would need a different notion of cover, and nothing here attempts one.

status.glance: Every stage of the roadmap has its stated targets proved. The universal cover is constructed, subgroups of `π₁(X, x₀)` classify connected covers in both pointed and unpointed form, covers are classified categorically with `π₁(X, x₀)` recovered as the automorphisms of the fibre functor, and the application list (`π₁(S¹)`, `π_n(S¹)`, tori, `K(G, 1)` recognition, `RPⁿ`) is complete. What remains lies beyond the roadmap's text: computing higher homotopy groups, and bases without a universal cover.
